title: Banks, The Fed And A Trailblazing BoJ
gist: Louis-Vincent Gave argues the Bank of Japan has been the first mover on every major unconventional monetary policy of the past 30 years - zero rates, quantitative easing, negative rates - each time to foreign surprise or disgust, and is now trailblazing again by deliberately sitting on its hands while inflation accelerates and the long end of the JGB market sells off.

themes.theme: BoJ as serial first mover in unconventional monetary policy

insights.claim: Over the past 30 years the Bank of Japan has almost always been the first major central bank to adopt unconventional monetary policy, pioneering zero interest rate policy, quantitative easing and negative interest rate policies before anyone else.
insights.speaker: Louis-Vincent Gave
insights.so_what: Treat BoJ policy experiments as a leading indicator for what the Fed and ECB eventually adopt, rather than as a Japan-only idiosyncrasy.
insights.quote: The BoJ was the first major central bank to embrace zero interest rate policies, the first to embrace quantitative easing, the first to embrace negative interest rate policies…

insights.claim: Each time the Bank of Japan broke new policy ground, the rest of the world reacted with surprise and sometimes even disgust at Japanese central bankers' actions - before eventually following.
insights.speaker: Louis-Vincent Gave
insights.so_what: Consensus revulsion at a BoJ policy move is historically a poor reason to dismiss it; it has been an early signal of the next global policy regime.

themes.theme: BoJ inaction amid rising inflation and a JGB long-end selloff

insights.claim: Over the past few years the Bank of Japan has deliberately sat on its hands even as Japanese inflation accelerated and the long end of the Japanese government bond market sold off.
insights.speaker: Louis-Vincent Gave
insights.so_what: A central bank tolerating both above-target inflation and a disorderly long-end selloff is a live template for financial repression; monitor 20-30yr JGB yields and the yen as the transmission channels.
insights.quote: the BoJ has sat on its hands as inflation accelerated and the long end of the Japanese government bond market sold off
insights.locator: In this spirit of unconventional policies

insights.claim: Central-bank passivity in the face of accelerating inflation and a steepening long end is framed as the newest form of unconventional policy, not as a policy error or oversight.
insights.speaker: Louis-Vincent Gave
insights.so_what: If inaction is intentional policy, bets on imminent BoJ tightening to defend the long end are mispriced; the pain trade is higher-for-longer JGB yields with no official pushback.
insights.quote: In this spirit of unconventional policies, over the past few years, the BoJ has sat on its hands
insights.locator: In this spirit of unconventional policies

insights.claim: The framing of a trailblazing Bank of Japan alongside banks and the Fed implies that the BoJ's current stance of tolerating inflation and a bond-market selloff could again be copied by other major central banks, with knock-on consequences for bank balance sheets.
insights.speaker: Louis-Vincent Gave
insights.so_what: Watch for the Fed adopting similar tolerance of long-end yields; banks holding long-duration government paper would be the first-order casualties and Japanese banks the early read-through.
